name: Epithelial barrier and junction maintenance
definition: Apical junctional complex: tight-junction strand proteins (claudins, occludin), cytoplasmic scaffolds (ZO-1/2/3, cingulin), and adherens/desmosomal adhesion molecules that set paracellular permeability of the nasal epithelium.
interpretation_note: A tighter barrier restricts pathogen and allergen penetration, but also restricts access of intranasally delivered antigen to subepithelial APCs; several mucosal adjuvants act by transiently loosening junctions. Higher score must not be read as 'better vaccine response'.
limitations: Transcript abundance is a weak proxy for assembled junction function (no TEER equivalent); junction proteins are heavily post-translationally regulated. Claudin family members are functionally opposed (sealing vs pore-forming), so a single summed score is directionally ambiguous. TJP3 and MARVELD2 returned no Reactome mapping.

name: Motile ciliary (mucociliary) machinery
definition: Axonemal structural and motility apparatus of multiciliated cells: outer/inner dynein arms, radial spokes, central apparatus, dynein assembly factors, plus the FOXJ1 multiciliogenesis transcriptional program.
anchor_go: GO:0060294 (cilium movement involved in cell motility)
anchor_reactome: R-HSA-9945556 (Transcriptional regulation of multiciliogenesis); R-HSA-5620924 (Intraflagellar transport) - coverage poor
interpretation_note: Efficient mucociliary clearance removes pathogens but equally removes intranasally delivered vaccine antigen, shortening mucosal residence time. Direction of benefit depends on formulation and residence requirements.
limitations: Reactome maps only 2/20 of these genes; evidence rests on GO annotations and primary-ciliary-dyskinesia genetics, much of it IEA or model-organism derived. mRNA level does not measure ciliary beat frequency or coordinated transport.

name: Airway mucin / secretory product panel (small panel)
definition: Gel-forming mucins and abundant secretory-cell products of the airway surface liquid.
interpretation_note: Mucus traps and clears antigen; it can also physically impede antigen uptake and vaccine delivery.
limitations: Only five genes, with extreme dynamic range and strong secretory-cell restriction; reported as a small panel, not as an enrichment signature. SCGB1A1 has no Reactome mapping. Counts for MUC5AC/MUC5B are poorly captured by 3'-biased scRNA-seq in real data. In the nasal epithelium SCGB1A1 is a weaker secretory marker than in the bronchi (nasal secretory cells express MUC4, PI3 and SIX3 instead), so it contributes little in nasal brushings.

name: Polymeric antibody transport (PIGR gene-level feature)
definition: Epithelial receptor-mediated transcytosis of dimeric IgA/pentameric IgM to the mucosal surface and release of secretory component.
anchor_go: GO:0002415 (immunoglobulin transcytosis in epithelial cells mediated by polymeric immunoglobulin receptor; PIGR IDA, PMID:10229845)
anchor_reactome: none - Reactome has no pIgR transcytosis pathway containing PIGR (PIGR mapped only to generic pathways)
interpretation_note: Transport capacity is necessary for secretory IgA to reach the lumen, so higher PIGR plausibly supports mucosal antibody delivery. It reports transport capacity only, not antigen-specific antibody.
limitations: Single gene: the 'score' is simply normalised PIGR expression and is reported as a gene-level feature, not an enrichment score. PIGR is induced by IFN-gamma, IL-17 and TNF, so its level also tracks inflammation. Airway-specific functional evidence cited here is from a pIgR-deficient mouse model (PMID 27046438); the human nasal evidence cited (PMID 41822483) is an association between nasal secretory IgA and viral shedding, not a measurement of PIGR transcript.

name: FcRn IgG transport (gene-level feature)
definition: Neonatal Fc receptor heavy chain mediating bidirectional IgG transcytosis and IgG/albumin recycling at epithelial surfaces.
anchor_go: GO:0002415-adjacent; FCGRT annotated to IgG transcytosis / IgG receptor activity
anchor_reactome: no module-specific pathway returned (FCGRT not mapped in this query)
interpretation_note: Relevant to IgG-mediated mucosal protection, which is a different effector arm from secretory IgA; grouping it with PIGR would merge two distinct transport systems.
limitations: Single gene, reported separately from PIGR; beta-2 microglobulin (B2M) is the obligate partner chain but is also an MHC-I component and is scored in M06.

name: Innate pathogen sensing (constitutive receptors and proximal adaptors)
definition: Pattern-recognition receptors (TLRs, STING, NLRs) and proximal adaptors/kinases up to IRF3. Sensors that are themselves interferon-stimulated genes (RIGI, IFIH1, DHX58, TLR3, AIM2, CGAS) are excluded so that the module is less of a proxy for interferon tone.
anchor_reactome: R-HSA-166016 (TLR4 cascade, 9/21); R-HSA-1834949 (Cytosolic sensors of pathogen-associated DNA, 8/21)
interpretation_note: Sensing capacity may support responsiveness to TLR/STING-agonist adjuvants, but also drives reactogenicity; it is not intrinsically beneficial.
limitations: Removing the canonical ISG sensors reduces but does not remove interferon dependence; check the donor-level correlation with M05 (nas.tl.module_correlation) before reading M04 as independent of ISG tone. TLR7 is expressed mainly by immune cells and is barely detected in airway epithelial cells, so in epithelium the module is carried by TLR2/4/5, NOD1/2, NLRP3 and the adaptors. MYD88, TBK1, TRAF3 and MAVS are broadly expressed. Expression of a receptor does not imply signalling competence.

name: Interferon-stimulated genes (type I and III interferon response)
definition: Canonical interferon-stimulated effector and amplifier genes downstream of IFNAR and IFNLR1 JAK-STAT signalling. At the airway epithelium type III interferon (IFN-lambda) induces largely the same genes as type I, so the module cannot tell the two apart.
interpretation_note: Higher baseline ISG tone has been reported in children's upper airways and is antiviral, but type I IFN is also immunopathological in other settings and can restrict replication of live-attenuated vaccines. A high score must not be labelled automatically beneficial.
limitations: Not specific to type I interferon: type III (dominant at the airway epithelium) and partly type II interferon induce the same genes. Baseline ISG tone largely reflects recent or ongoing respiratory viral exposure rather than a stable trait; without viral testing it is unattributable.

name: MHC class I antigen processing and peptide loading
definition: Immunoproteasome subunits, peptide transport into the ER, the peptide-loading complex, and MHC-I heavy/light chains.
anchor_go: GO:0019885 (antigen processing and presentation of endogenous peptide antigen via MHC class I)
anchor_reactome: R-HSA-983170 (Antigen Presentation: Folding, assembly and peptide loading of class I MHC, 11/15)
interpretation_note: Relevant to CD8 T-cell priming/recall, but PSMB8, PSMB9, TAP1 and B2M are themselves interferon-inducible, so a high score may simply reflect interferon tone (M05) rather than independent presentation capacity.
limitations: Strong overlap with the interferon module by biology, not by gene sharing; HLA-A/B/C mapping in real data is confounded by allelic reference bias (not reproduced in this simulation). Immunoproteasome, TAP and NLRC5 are interferon-inducible, so M06 tracks M05; check nas.tl.module_correlation. HLA-A/B/C are polymorphic and align to the reference genome with allele-dependent efficiency, so scores partly reflect HLA type and ancestry; rerun with nas.drop_hla() as a sensitivity analysis. HLA-A/B/C and B2M are among the most highly expressed genes in most cells, so UCell scores can sit near their ceiling (see the score_distribution table).

name: MHC class II antigen processing and presentation
definition: Class II alpha/beta chains, invariant chain, HLA-DM editing, CIITA transactivation and the endolysosomal proteases that generate class II peptides.
anchor_go: GO:0019886 (antigen processing and presentation of exogenous peptide antigen via MHC class II)
interpretation: supportive in professional APC; context-dependent in epithelium
interpretation_note: In dendritic cells, macrophages and B cells this reports classical CD4 priming machinery. Airway and nasal epithelial cells can express HLA-DR and CD86 under inflammatory/IFN-gamma conditions, but epithelial class II expression is not evidence of professional APC function and is scored and interpreted separately.
limitations: CIITA and CTSS are expressed well below the class II structural genes, so the score is dominated by HLA-D* and CD74 abundance. Epithelial class II is inducible and cannot be distinguished from professional APC function by transcript level alone. HLA class II genes are highly polymorphic; reference-alignment bias makes scores partly reflect HLA type and ancestry. Rerun with nas.drop_hla() as a sensitivity analysis. LGMN has no verified supporting reference in references.csv.

name: Professional APC costimulation and maturation
definition: B7-family and TNF-superfamily costimulatory ligands plus the non-canonical NF-kB maturation axis and DC maturation markers.
anchor_reactome: R-HSA-389356 (CD28 co-stimulation; CD80, CD86); R-HSA-5668541 (TNFR2 non-canonical NF-kB pathway, 6/12)
interpretation_note: Costimulatory ligand availability is a limiting factor for naive T-cell priming, so higher levels are plausibly supportive; however, high baseline costimulation may equally mark ongoing local inflammation.
limitations: Mixed content: CD83, CCR7, LAMP3, RELB and NFKB2 are maturation/migration markers rather than costimulatory ligands, so the module conflates ligand availability with maturation state. CD83, ICOSLG, CCR7 and LAMP3 returned no mapping to the two anchor pathways. Restricted to professional APC populations. CCR7, LAMP3, CD80, CD86 and CD40 together mark the mature/regulatory DC state, so in a dendritic population that pools cDC1, cDC2, pDC and mature DCs the score largely measures the mature-DC fraction. Annotate DC subtypes and keep them as subtypes so the analysis can adjust for subtype fractions.

name: Plasma-cell secretory machinery
definition: Plasma-cell differentiation regulators (PRDM1, XBP1, IRF4) and the ER/secretory apparatus that supports high-rate antibody secretion (MZB1, DERL3, SEC11C, SSR4, FKBP11), plus the plasma-cell survival receptor BCMA (TNFRSF17). Immunoglobulin constant-region genes and JCHAIN are excluded: isotype is scored separately (M10), and Ig transcripts are the commonest ambient contaminant in nasal samples.
anchor_go: GO:0002381 (immunoglobulin production involved in immunoglobulin-mediated immune response); GO:0071751 (secretory IgA immunoglobulin complex)
anchor_reactome: poor coverage - MZB1 and FKBP11 unmapped; only R-HSA-9938027 (Affinity selection of immunoglobulins, 3/12)
interpretation_note: JCHAIN is required for polymeric IgA assembly and therefore couples this module mechanistically to PIGR-mediated transport; both are needed for secretory IgA.
limitations: Measures the secretory programme of the plasma cells recovered, not antibody output or specificity. Plasma cells are rare in brushings, so few donors may reach the minimum cell count. Within plasma cells these genes are very highly expressed, so check the score_distribution table for ceiling effects.

name: IgA share of immunoglobulin heavy-chain transcripts (ratio feature)
definition: Donor-level fraction of IgA heavy-chain counts (IGHA1+IGHA2) among all IgA, IgG and IgM heavy-chain counts in the cell population, reported on the logit scale. Not a UCell score.
anchor_go: not assigned (no verified GO/Reactome anchor recorded)
anchor_reactome: not assigned (no verified GO/Reactome anchor recorded)
interpretation_note: Secretory IgA is the main antibody at the nasal mucosal surface; a shift from IgA towards IgG among local plasma cells changes the type of antibody available there. It does not measure antigen-specific antibody.
limitations: Computed from pooled counts, so it is dominated by the cells with the most Ig transcript. Ambient Ig contamination comes mostly from plasma cells themselves, which limits but does not remove bias. IGHD and IGHE are not included.

name: Senescence-associated cell-cycle arrest
definition: Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitors that enforce senescence-associated arrest (p21/CDKN1A, p16/CDKN2A) plus secreted factors reported in senescent cells and ageing plasma (SERPINE1/PAI-1, IGFBP7, GDF15).
anchor_go: not assigned (no verified GO/Reactome anchor recorded)
anchor_reactome: not assigned (no verified GO/Reactome anchor recorded)
interpretation_note: Senescent epithelial and immune cells accumulate with age and may alter mucosal repair and responses. A transcript score is not a diagnosis of senescence.
limitations: No single transcript defines senescence. CDKN1A is also induced by p53 activation, DNA damage and interferon (it is in the interferon-stimulated gene library), and CDKN2A mRNA is low and unreliably detected in scRNA-seq; for these reasons the SenMayo gene set deliberately excludes both. p16- and p21-positive cells were not found to increase with age in human lung. Read the module as an arrest-associated programme, not as a count of senescent cells.

name: Inflammatory cytokines (SASP / inflammaging core)
definition: Pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines that form the core of the senescence-associated secretory phenotype and of age-associated chronic low-grade inflammation (inflammaging).
anchor_go: not assigned (no verified GO/Reactome anchor recorded)
anchor_reactome: not assigned (no verified GO/Reactome anchor recorded)
interpretation_note: Chronic low-grade inflammation is a hallmark of ageing, but the same cytokines rise acutely with infection, allergy, smoking and sampling trauma.
limitations: Cytokine transcripts are sparse and bursty in scRNA-seq, so the per-donor mean is used (aggregation 'auto'). Acute infection and sampling stress are strong confounders; brushing itself can induce immediate-early inflammatory genes.

name: Tissue-resident memory T-cell core programme
definition: Genes of the human tissue-resident memory T-cell (TRM) core signature (Kumar et al. 2017): residency/retention markers (CD69, CD103/ITGAE, CD49a/ITGA1), the CXCR6 chemokine receptor, and PDCD1, CRTAM and DUSP6.
anchor_go: not assigned (no verified GO/Reactome anchor recorded)
anchor_reactome: not assigned (no verified GO/Reactome anchor recorded)
interpretation_note: Resident memory T cells in the airway mucosa provide rapid local protection, and their maintenance changes with age.
limitations: CD69 is also an early activation marker, so residency should not be inferred from CD69 alone. ITGAE (CD103) marks CD8+ TRM much more than CD4+ TRM, so the score leans towards CD8 cells; annotate CD4 and CD8 T cells as subtypes so the model adjusts for their mix. Scored only in T cells.
